title: Slyde
tagline: A presentation studio that knows your company — so every pitch starts from your best work, not a blank slide.

body: Teams lose days rebuilding the same presentations. Their best decks, case studies and positioning live in old files and people's heads, so every new pitch starts from a blank slide — and the tools that promise speed hand back something generic that doesn't sound like the company at all.

I wanted to fix that end to end: one place that holds what a company knows and how it talks, and turns it into on-brand presentations in its own templates — fast enough for a same-day RFP, good enough to send.

The answer is a company Brain. Slyde gathers a team's past decks, case studies, website and voice into an organized knowledge base, then builds new presentations from it — a brief goes in, a finished deck in the company's own templates comes out. That idea shaped the positioning and the line that leads the brand: "Stop being generic. Use your brain."

Around it sits a complete product: a Keynote-grade editor with smart guides and charts, real-time collaboration with live cursors, chat, comments and assignments, a slide library the whole team can search, PowerPoint and PDF import, editable PowerPoint export, and workspaces with roles and paid plans. I led all of it — the vision, the product and design calls, and every feature review — across more than 2,800 commits.

The brand was mine end to end: the name (DeckForge, then Slydra, then Slyde), three design systems that landed on Product Pop's violet and paper, the messaging and the marketing site. I directed the launch film like any shoot — concept, script, look and edit — built in Blender and After Effects and taken through 146 versions until every frame landed.
